claims.quote: The solute carrier family 6 member 1 (SLC6A1) gene encodes the γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporter GAT-1
the deficiency of which is associated with infantile encephalopathy with intellectual disability.
conducted preclinical gene therapy studies using heterozygous and homozygous Slc6a1-KO mice

claims.object_text: AAV9 vectors with JeT or MeP promoter (neonatal intracerebroventricular administration)
claims.quote: Neonatal intracerebroventricular administration of either vector resulted in significantly normalized EEG patterns in Slc6a1-/- or Slc6a1+/- mice as well as improvement in several behavioral phenotypes of Slc6a1-/- mice.

claims.object_text: Intrathecal administration of AAV9 vectors at P5
claims.quote: Intrathecal administration of either vector at P5 normalized EEG patterns in Slc6a1+/- mice

claims.object_text: Intrathecal administration of AAV9 vectors at P5
claims.quote: but in Slc6a1-/- mice, the treatment only rescued nest building without impact on EEG.
Both vectors were well tolerated in all mice treated at P5 or later (including WT mice), up to 1 year after injection.

claims.object_text: AAV9/SLC6A1 treatments outside the neonatal window
claims.quote: outside of the neonatal treatment window, the severe homozygous KO model is more refractory to treatment, whereas our treatments in the heterozygous mice, which genotypically match human patients, have resulted in stronger benefits.
